applies_why: The judge text addresses a collision between the challenger's Romans 1:3 descent claim and the defender's Holy-Ghost-conception chain, so it is the kind of chain-against-chain collision K-C governs.
quote: without explicit textual resolution of paternity
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words': one reading allows UNDERDETERMINED when no verse explicitly resolves paternity; the other reading makes absence of explicit contrary wording irrelevant to the required chain-against-chain footing.
why: The judge text rests the UNDERDETERMINED label on lack of explicit textual resolution of paternity, which is the retired stating-verse/no-explicit-contrary test rather than chain-against-chain footing.
